context: Set theory: ordered pairs and Kuratowski encoding, not an unordered doubleton
editorial_note: Direct ProofWiki formalization and alternative Wiener/empty-set encodings read. Alternative encodings have equivalent coordinate behavior, but are not equal as sets and need separately labeled representations.
potential_contextual_variants: ordered coordinates with equality iff corresponding coordinates equal
other set encodings with same coordinate uniqueness
text: An ordered pair (a,b) records a first coordinate a and a second coordinate b. One rigorous set-theoretic implementation is the Kuratowski pair (a,b):={{a},{a,b}}, whose equality agrees with coordinatewise equality.

context: Set theory: non-strict subset relation for arbitrary sets
editorial_note: ProofWiki uses ⊆ for non-strict inclusion and distinguishes proper subset. Do not imply the class of all sets is itself a set or confuse ⊂ notation conventions.
text: For sets A and B, A is a subset of B, written A⊆B, precisely when every x∈A is also an element of B. Proper inclusion A⊊B additionally requires A≠B.

context: Set theory: total single-valued map X→Y, typed graph, bare graph with ambient carriers
editorial_note: ProofWiki Definition 1 uses total single-valued assignment; Definitions 2–3 use a typed relation (X,Y,G) and equivalent total and uniqueness axioms. The bare graph G does not by itself determine the codomain Y. Distinguish typed mapping data from bare graph equality.
potential_contextual_variants: typed graph with totality and single-valuedness
bare graph subset under fixed ambient sets
text: For sets X,Y, a mapping f:X→Y assigns each x∈X exactly one y∈Y. Equivalently, with X and Y specified, its graph G⊆X×Y satisfies: for every x∈X exactly one y∈Y has (x,y)∈G.
